findings: High: The current composition is still catalog-first, not graph-first. The top-level shell is a family grid, then a separate lane-based model map, then an examples strip, while the `Architectures` tab is a distinct card catalog and `Route evidence` is a separate table ([index.html](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/index.html#L72), [index.html](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/index.html#L101), [index.html](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/index.html#L116), [app.js](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js#L137), [app.js](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js#L168), [app.js](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js#L193), [app.js](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js#L260)). There is no explicit root node, no edge layer, and no shared ancestry visualization for `root -> family -> subtype -> model`.

High: Multi-family models are represented as repeated lane pills rather than a single readable identity node. The data has 111 models, 489 routes, five carrier families, fifteen subtypes, and 45 multi-family models, with one model spanning four families. Current lane nodes are truncated to 260px and only show `model name + family route count`, so multi-family identity and route provenance are easy to lose ([app.js](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js#L168), [styles.css](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/styles.css#L461), [styles.css](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/styles.css#L495)).

High: Route-level detail is pushed into secondary surfaces instead of the focus interaction. The only deep route view is the modal dialog and the paginated evidence table, which is horizontally wide and table-based; that makes route inspection feel detached from the hierarchy the user is trying to understand ([app.js](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js#L282), [app.js](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js#L327), [app.js](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js#L360), [styles.css](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/styles.css#L762), [styles.css](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/styles.css#L887)). For the requested design, route detail needs to emerge from node focus, not from a separate evidence page.

Medium: The model-node media treatment does not yet satisfy the requested evidence/example split. The build pipeline copies a whole source figure image and stores caption/description metadata, but it does not record crop geometry or panel selection; the current model cards also show the whole figure asset, while the small illustrative input examples live in a separate subtype example list ([build_input_representation_atlas.py](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/scripts/build_input_representation_atlas.py#L315), [build_input_representation_atlas.py](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/scripts/build_input_representation_atlas.py#L367), [app.js](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js#L225), [app.js](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/app.js#L193)). That means the current atlas cannot yet place a tightly relevant source-image crop and a clearly labeled example input inside the same model node as requested.

Medium: Mobile behavior is acceptable for a catalog, but not for a graph-first hierarchy. The current responsive rules collapse the family grid, architecture grid, and route pipeline into stacked layouts, but the primary evidence table still requires `min-width: 980px`, and the overview retains wide, separate sections rather than a compact hierarchical drill-down ([styles.css](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/styles.css#L1209), [styles.css](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/styles.css#L1262), [styles.css](/Users/bogdan.didenko/lpnu/review/docs/input-representation-atlas/assets/styles.css#L768)). On phones, the primary graph should become a vertical accordion/tree and the evidence table should be secondary and collapsible, not the main path.
recommended_graph: Root node: `Input representation atlas` -> five carrier-family nodes -> fifteen subtype nodes -> 111 model nodes. Make ancestry explicit with a single shared node identity per model and allow multiple inbound edges for multi-family models instead of duplicating the model as separate nodes.

Use a layered web graph, not a canvas diagram: render nodes with CSS grid or flex rails and draw edges with SVG underneath or between columns. Keep the hierarchy visible as `root -> family -> subtype -> model`, and let focus reveal route-level cards on the right or in a bottom sheet.

Interaction model: hover or tap highlights one ancestry path and dims the rest; clicking a family expands/collapses its subtypes; clicking a subtype filters to its routes; clicking a model opens a focused detail pane that steps through that model's grounded routes one at a time.

Model node content: include the model name, route count, family chips, and a compact family-aware label block. Inside the node, show a tightly relevant source-figure crop as the evidence image and a separate, small `Example input` strip as the explanatory example. Label them explicitly so the evidence crop is not confused with the illustrative example.

Multi-family treatment: keep a single model node, but stack its family badges and show all parent edges. If the node becomes crowded, cap visible badges at two and move the remainder into an expandable `+N families` chip or tooltip.

Secondary surfaces: keep the architecture catalog and evidence table available, but demote them to search/filter result panels that are populated from the graph selection. The graph should be the entry point; the table should be the audit trail.
risks: Without crop coordinates or panel-level metadata, the build cannot deliver the requested evidence-image crop reliably; it will keep falling back to full-figure thumbnails.
A single node per multi-family model will get visually dense if all routes are rendered at once; route chips need progressive disclosure to avoid turning the graph into a text wall.
On mobile, explicit SVG edges can become cluttered fast; the layout needs a simplified stacked mode with collapse/expand affordances and a persistent focused-detail sheet.
If explanatory examples are not visually separated from grounded source imagery, readers may misread the synthetic input example as evidence from the paper figure.
acceptance_checks: The primary view contains one explicit root and exactly 5 family nodes, 15 subtype nodes, and 111 model nodes, with ancestry visible as `root -> family -> subtype -> model`.
A multi-family model appears once as one identity node, not as duplicated catalog entries, and shows multiple incoming family/subtype links.
Clicking a family or subtype changes the graph focus and reveals the corresponding routes inline or in a side panel; route-level details are reachable without opening the evidence table first.

Each model node contains two clearly labeled media treatments: a grounded crop from the original paper figure and a small illustrative example of the actual model input; the two must not be visually conflated.
The evidence table and catalog remain available but are secondary to the graph, and on mobile the primary graph does not require horizontal scrolling to understand the hierarchy.
All node, edge, and focus states remain usable on touch devices, with readable labels for multi-family models and no truncation that hides the model identity.
